slides.text: The old bookstore had one strange rule: every customer could leave exactly one sealed letter on a shelf labeled 'For Tomorrow.' Nobody was allowed to read them. Nobody knew who collected them. Every Friday, a woman in a yellow sweater would quietly leave another envelope. She had done it for almost twenty years without missing a single week.

Curiosity finally defeated me. After she left, I asked the owner who the letters were for. He smiled sadly. 'Her husband. He was diagnosed with Alzheimer's before they married. They agreed that when he forgot who she was, she'd keep introducing herself—one letter at a time.' The owner handed me the oldest envelope. It simply read, 'Hi love, I'm Emma.'

Months later I saw them together outside the shop. He looked confused as she gently handed him another letter. He opened it, smiled, and offered her his arm. 'You seem wonderful,' he said. She laughed through tears. 'You'll think that every Friday.' Then they walked away like two strangers beginning the greatest love story for the hundredth time.
